01

How to use this tab

This tab is the working surface for shortening and repairing the instrument. The Pilot 3 tab tells the story of the field; this one lists every page and every question with the numbers a cut decision needs, computed once from the same rows.

  1. Find the minutes. Every page is costed in median active seconds per complete, with seconds per item so a 36-row matrix and a one-item page compare fairly. The ten most expensive pages hold 7.7 of the 19.0 summed page-median minutes.
  2. Set a target and test cuts. The cut simulator recomputes each complete’s remaining active time when you untick pages, so the new median is the real median, not a sum of medians. Reaching a 15-minute median from today’s 22.0 means removing about 7.0 minutes per person.
  3. Grade the questions. Every question carries coverage, non-response, distribution shape, straight-lining, its strongest correlate outside its battery, time per item and voice yield, with flags you can filter on. Expand a row to see the answer distribution with option labels.
  4. Merge what overlaps. The redundancy map lists item pairs with |Spearman r| ≥ .6 and the reliability of every multi-row battery; a construct that is predictable from another is a candidate to drop or to keep as a single item.
  5. Collapse what nobody picks. Response options lists the options under 3%, the don’t-know shares and the slider pile-ups.
  6. Check the qualitative yield. Open-ends shows, per item, how many answer, by voice or keyboard, at what length, and how many say “nothing”.

Base for everything below unless stated: the 307 completes of the Bovitz pilot (Forthright rid present, hub-served, one row per rid, team and smoke rows excluded). Item statistics use the completes shown each item; page timings use active dwell (the tab in the foreground), not wall-clock. The field was still open at generation; parked rows can still convert.

02

Where the minutes go

Median active time for a complete is 22.0 minutes (p25 15.7, p75 31.4). Summing every page’s median gives 19.0 minutes; the two differ because slow people are slow on different pages.

04

Where people quit

84 landing-clearers are parked mid-survey (20% of 429 clearers), 38 were terminated by the attention row on page 7, 307 completed. The curve shows who is still in at each page; the bars normalise quits by the people who reached the page, which is what separates a page that repels from a page that merely sits early.

05

Cut simulator

Untick pages to remove them. The simulator drops each complete’s recorded seconds on those pages and recomputes the distribution of remaining active time over the 307 completes, so the result is a real median, not a sum of medians. It assumes the remaining pages keep their timings, which holds for cuts but not for reordering.

Every item in this build is required, so item non-response is not a signal here; a “gates” chip marks the variables whose answers decide which later questions appear.

Method and caveats

Rows. Supabase audseg_survey_responses, survey_id audseg-w2-final, capture time at or after 2026-09-11T16:00:43Z (the republish of build 6ec1f17a), metadata.instrumentVersion = 6ec1f17a, panel provider Forthright with a respondent id, served from the hub. Excluded at this cut: 0 rows without a rid and 1 smoke rows (team checks), 0 localhost row(s); 3 duplicate row(s) folded to one per rid (complete row preferred, else the latest). Result: 482 arrivals, 429 past the landing (251 spoke the phrase, 178 typed it), 38 attention terminations, 307 completes, 84 parked.

Time. Active dwell is the engine’s per-page activeMs (foreground time), summed over pages for a person. Page medians are over completes who saw the page. Items per page count matrix rows shown, wall cards shown and rotated questions shown for that person; seconds per item divides the page median by the median item count. The cut simulator drops each complete’s recorded seconds on the unticked pages and recomputes the distribution.

Shown and answered. A question counts as shown when the person saw its page, the rotation record (_pm_questions_*) includes it, and its branching condition evaluates true on their stored answers; matrix rows use the per-person _pm_matrix_* / _pipedrows_* records. Non-response is shown minus answered; most items are required, so non-response mainly appears on open-ends and on rows a person could leave blank.

Shape. Distributions list the configured options in display order with counts and shares. Means and SDs use the numeric option codes, excluding don’t-know / not-applicable style options; sliders are binned for display but summarized on raw values. Straight-lining counts people who gave the identical answer to every row on a matrix that showed them at least three rows.

Correlations. Spearman on pairwise-complete answers (n ≥ 60 for the map, ≥ 30 within batteries). “Best r outside” is the strongest correlate outside the item’s own battery. Standardized α = k·r̄ / (1 + (k−1)·r̄) with k the designed row count. The heatmap uses single-item numeric questions with at least 100 answers.

Flags. low variance: one answer holds ≥70% of responses (≥3-point scales): the item barely separates people, unless it gates other questions; opt-out heavy: ≥15% chose a don’t-know / not-applicable style option; rare options: at least one substantive option drew <3% (5- to 12-option scales): collapse candidate; pile-up: on a slider or count input, ≥25% sit at an endpoint or ≥20% at the exact midpoint; non-response: ≥5% of people shown the item left it blank; thin n: fewer than 60 answers at this snapshot (planned missingness, branching, or a late page); straightlining: ≥20% of people gave the identical answer to every row shown (≥4-point scales, ≥3 rows); rows redundant: mean inter-row Spearman r ≥ .6: rows say the same thing; redundant: |Spearman r| ≥ .7 with an item outside its own battery; non-substantive: ≥20% of answers are “none / nothing / don’t know” style; mostly empty: ≥30% of people tapped nothing on the wall; costly page: page median active seconds in the slowest tenth of pages; no answers: no stored answers among people shown the item.

Caveats. The field was open at generation; parked rows can still convert and would lower the hazard figures. Order effects are not separable from content effects in a single-order field: an early page pays a novelty cost and a late page a fatigue cost. Correlations on rotated batteries rest on small overlaps. Nothing here is weighted.
